what_its_for: Metoprolol is used to treat high blood pressure, chest pain (angina), and heart failure. It is also used after a heart attack to help protect your heart. It works by slowing your heart rate and helping your heart beat more regularly and with less effort.
how_to_take: Take metoprolol exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the extended-release tablet (Toprol-XL) whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. The regular tablet (Lopressor) can be split if needed. Take it with or right after a meal to help your body absorb it better. Try to take it at the same time every day.
dosing: Your dose depends on what condition is being treated and how you respond to the medicine. Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose and slowly increase it. Common doses range from 25 mg to 200 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Do not stop taking metoprolol suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can be dangerous for your heart.
storage: Store metoprolol at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can increase dizziness or lower your blood pressure too much. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without your doctor's approval — stopping abruptly can cause chest pain or a heart attack. Be careful when standing up quickly, as metoprolol can cause dizziness. Avoid driving or using heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements, especially cold medicines containing decongestants.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: a very slow heartbeat (fewer than 50 beats per minute), shortness of breath or new or worsening swelling in your legs or feet, sudden weight gain, feeling faint or passing out, severe dizziness, chest pain, or signs of depression such as feelings of sadness or mood changes. If you have symptoms of a serious allergic reaction — such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing — call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately.
when_it_works: Metoprolol starts working within a few hours of your first dose, but it may take several weeks before you feel the full benefit, especially for blood pressure control. Even if you feel well, keep taking it as prescribed. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so it is important not to stop the medicine just because you feel fine.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and slow heart rate, so extra caution is advised. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking this medicine. People with asthma, COPD, or certain heart conditions should use metoprolol with caution and must inform their doctor. Patients with diabetes should monitor blood sugar closely, as metoprolol may mask some signs of low blood sugar such as a fast heartbeat.
